name: KIT (white spotting)
summary: The white-spotting neighbourhood on chromosome 3, here an eight-allele locus covering sabino (SB1), the numbered dominant-white (W) series and the W20 booster. Coverage runs from a few white hairs to an almost entirely white horse. Because it is one locus, a horse is one of these and never two at once; some W homozygotes cannot occur.

phenotypes.name: Minimal white
phenotypes.description: Ordinary-looking white: a star or snip and a low sock or two, the sort of marking nobody would call a pattern. This is what a single booster copy - W20, W35, W32 or W34 - usually does on its own. They are boosters, and they show properly beside another variant.

phenotypes.name: Modest white
phenotypes.description: A little more than ordinary: a narrow blaze, socks climbing past the fetlock, maybe a fleck under the belly. Two booster copies are viable - the same one twice or two different ones - and do add white, but not reliably twice as much as one.

phenotypes.name: Sabino
phenotypes.description: Classic sabino: tall jagged stockings, white up the belly, a broad blaze, and roaned ragged margins rather than the clean edge a splash marking leaves.

phenotypes.name: Broad white spotting
phenotypes.description: Sabino carried much further: irregular white well up the legs and flanks, a wide blaze or bald face, and the first real patches on the barrel.

phenotypes.name: Extensive white
phenotypes.description: Most of the horse is white, with colour holding out over the topline, the crest and the quarters. The margins are still ragged - this is a very white spotted horse, not a white one.

phenotypes.name: Near-white
phenotypes.description: Ninety per cent white or more, with a few coloured flecks left on the ears and the crest. Sabino-white, and where the strong W alleles land when they meet each other.

phenotypes.name: Dominant white
phenotypes.description: Every pigment gone over the whole body and pink skin underneath, so the horse renders pure white and no other coat gene it carries can be seen. This is an absence of pigment cells, not a great deal of sabino.

phenotypes.name: Camarillo white
phenotypes.description: White from birth over the whole body, with pink skin underneath - not a grey that turned white, and not a great deal of sabino. Every other coat gene it carries is hidden and still inherited. Unlike the other all-white variant at this locus, two copies are not known to be nonviable.

phenotypes.name: Speckled white
phenotypes.description: White flecks and mottling scattered through the coat, thickest low on the body and thinning toward the topline, with a white face - not the torn-edged patches of sabino. The Icelandic word for it is yruskjottur.
